stem: Give one chemical test each to distinguish (i) propanal and propanone, (ii) benzoic acid and phenol.
model_answer:
(i) **Tollens' test:** propanal gives a silver mirror; propanone does not. (Or iodoform test: propanone gives a yellow precipitate; propanal does not.) [1]
(ii) **$\ce{NaHCO3}$ test:** benzoic acid gives brisk effervescence of $\ce{CO2}$; phenol does not. (Or neutral $\ce{FeCl3}$: phenol gives a violet colour.) [1]

stem: Give reasons: (i) the $\alpha$-hydrogen atoms of aldehydes and ketones are acidic; (ii) chloroethanoic acid is a stronger acid than ethanoic acid.
model_answer:
(i) The carbonyl group withdraws electrons strongly, and the carbanion (enolate ion) left after losing the $\alpha$-hydrogen is stabilised by resonance. [1]
(ii) Chlorine has a $-I$ effect; it disperses the negative charge of the carboxylate ion and stabilises it. [1]

(ii) Chlorine has a $-I$ effect; it disperses the negative charge of the carboxylate ion and stabilises it.

hint: Look at what stabilises the anion left behind in each case.

stem: Write the mechanism of the addition of HCN to a carbonyl compound. Why is a trace of base added?
model_answer:
**Step 1:** the base generates the nucleophile: $\ce{HCN + OH- <=> CN- + H2O}$ [½]
**Step 2** (slow): $\ce{CN-}$ attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon; the carbon changes from sp$^2$ to sp$^3$, giving a tetrahedral alkoxide intermediate $>$ $\ce{C(O^-)CN}$ [1]
**Step 3** (fast): the intermediate takes a proton to give the cyanohydrin $>$ $\ce{C(OH)CN}$ [½]
HCN is a weak acid and reacts very slowly on its own; the base produces $\ce{CN-}$, a much stronger nucleophile, and speeds up the reaction. [1]

**Step 3** (fast): the intermediate takes a proton to give the cyanohydrin $>$ $\ce{C(OH)CN}$

hint: The nucleophile is CN⁻. Ask where it comes from.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
Give reasons:
(i) Benzoic acid does not undergo the Friedel–Crafts reaction.
(ii) Only one of the two $\ce{-NH2}$ groups of semicarbazide reacts with carbonyl compounds.
(iii) Carboxylic acids are stronger acids than phenols.
model_answer:
(i) The $\ce{-COOH}$ group deactivates the ring, and the catalyst $\ce{AlCl3}$ (a Lewis acid) bonds to the carboxyl group. [1]
(ii) In $\ce{H2N-NH-CO-NH2}$ the $\ce{-NH2}$ attached directly to $\ce{C=O}$ has its lone pair delocalised by resonance with the carbonyl group, so it is not nucleophilic; only the other $\ce{-NH2}$ reacts. [1]
(iii) The carboxylate ion has two *equivalent* resonance structures with the negative charge on the two electronegative oxygen atoms. In phenoxide the structures are not equivalent and place charge on less electronegative carbon. So carboxylate is more stabilised. [1]

scheme.step: (i) The $\ce{-COOH}$ group deactivates the ring, and the catalyst $\ce{AlCl3}$ (a Lewis acid) bonds to the carboxyl group.

(ii) In $\ce{H2N-NH-CO-NH2}$ the $\ce{-NH2}$ attached directly to $\ce{C=O}$ has its lone pair delocalised by resonance with the carbonyl group, so it is not nucleophilic; only the other $\ce{-NH2}$ reacts.

(iii) The carboxylate ion has two *equivalent* resonance structures with the negative charge on the two electronegative oxygen atoms. In phenoxide the structures are not equivalent and place charge on less electronegative carbon. So carboxylate is more stabilised.

hint: (i) What does AlCl₃ bind to? (ii) Which nitrogen lone pairs are tied up by resonance with C=O? (iii) Dimers.

label: PYQ-style
stem:
(a) Write the structures and names of the products formed when propanal is treated with dilute NaOH and the product is then heated. [2]
(b) Write the product of the reaction of benzaldehyde with acetophenone in dilute NaOH at 293 K. [1]
(c) Give reasons: (i) methanal undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction but ethanal does not; (ii) methanoic acid is a stronger acid than ethanoic acid. [2]
model_answer:
(a) $\ce{2CH3CH2CHO ->[dil. NaOH]}$
$\ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH(CH3)CHO}$ — 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal [1]
$\ce{->[\Delta][-H2O] CH3CH2CH=C(CH3)CHO}$ — 2-methylpent-2-enal [1]
(b) $\ce{C6H5CHO + C6H5COCH3 ->[dil. NaOH][293 K]}$
$\ce{C6H5CH=CH-CO-C6H5 + H2O}$ — 1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one (benzalacetophenone); a cross aldol condensation. [1]
(c)(i) Methanal has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, so with concentrated alkali it disproportionates (Cannizzaro). Ethanal has $\alpha$-hydrogens and undergoes aldol condensation instead. [1]
(ii) The $\ce{-CH3}$ group of ethanoic acid has a +I effect, which intensifies the negative charge on the carboxylate ion and destabilises it; methanoate has no such group. [1]

scheme.step: (a) $\ce{2CH3CH2CHO ->[dil. NaOH]}$ $\ce{CH3CH2CH(OH)CH(CH3)CHO}$ — 3-hydroxy-2-methylpentanal
$\ce{->[\Delta][-H2O] CH3CH2CH=C(CH3)CHO}$ — 2-methylpent-2-enal
(b) $\ce{C6H5CHO + C6H5COCH3 ->[dil. NaOH][293 K]}$ $\ce{C6H5CH=CH-CO-C6H5 + H2O}$ — 1,3-diphenylprop-2-en-1-one (benzalacetophenone); a cross aldol condensation.
(c)(i) Methanal has no $\alpha$-hydrogen, so with concentrated alkali it disproportionates (Cannizzaro). Ethanal has $\alpha$-hydrogens and undergoes aldol condensation instead.
(ii) The $\ce{-CH3}$ group of ethanoic acid has a +I effect, which intensifies the negative charge on the carboxylate ion and destabilises it; methanoate has no such group.

hint: Propanal has α-hydrogens: aldol addition first, then loss of water on heating.
